newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel in bid to tighten grip over East Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: Israel in bid to tighten grip over East Jerusalem.

text.p: Israel decided on Sunday to allocate $39 million to strengthen the Jewish state's hold over East Jerusalem, where Palestinians hope to establish the capital of a future state.

A government statement said the funds would be used to improve infrastructure in Arab East Jerusalem, which Israel says is an eternal and inseparable part of its capital, and to prevent "foreign political and diplomatic activity" in the city.

"The government of Israel will act to strengthen Israeli sovereignty in Jerusalem and for this purpose will allocate the necessary resources," said the statement issued after a meeting of the ministerial committee on Jerusalem headed by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
"Through law enforcement and political and security measures Israel will prevent any foreign political and diplomatic activity in Jerusalem which is against Israeli law," it said.

Israel captured East Jerusalem in the 1967 Middle East war along with the rest of the West Bank and Gaza Strip. It later annexed the eastern part of the city, home to Judaism's sacred Western Wall and the al-Aqsa mosque complex, Islam's third holiest site.

Under interim Israeli-PLO peace deals that launched Palestinian self-rule in parts of the West Bank and Gaza, the fate of the holy city is to be negotiated in "final status" peace talks due to be completed by May 1999.

Netanyahu's government says PLO political activity in Jerusalem is illegal and contradicts interim peace deals. Palestinians accuse Israel of establishing "facts on the ground" ahead of the final status talks.

"The ministerial committee...approved the mayor's request to allocate a special budget for East Jerusalem to facilitate improvements in infrastructure, developing roads, building schools, solving problems of drainage, sewage and more," said a Jerusalem municipality spokeswoman.
She said most of the money would come from the Treasury and other government offices.
